subtopics.title: The Two Original Participants — Households and Firms

questions.question: In the circular flow, households are defined as:
options: The owners of ALL factors of production — natural resources, labour, capital and entrepreneurship
The units that produce goods and services
The buyers in the factor market

questions.question: Firms pay households factor incomes, matched correctly as:
options: Profit for labour, wages for capital
Wages for labour, rent for natural resources, interest for capital, profit for entrepreneurship
Interest for labour, rent for entrepreneurship
One combined salary for all factors

questions.question: REAL flows and MONEY flows relate as follows:
options: Both travel in the same direction
Real flows exist only in barter economies
Real flows are physical things — factors and goods — and every one has a money flow travelling the OPPOSITE way
Money flows exist only in the goods market

subtopics.title: Leakages and Injections — Why the Circle Shrinks and Grows

questions.question: A LEAKAGE is:
options: Income that escapes the spending stream instead of returning to firms — savings is the first example

questions.question: INVESTMENT in the circular flow means:
options: Buying shares on the stock exchange
Firms' spending on capital goods — machinery, vehicles, buildings — financed largely through borrowed savings
Any purchase by a wealthy household
Money kept in a fixed deposit

questions.question: When total leakages EXCEED total injections:
options: Less money returns to firms each round — production, incomes and the whole circle contract

questions.question: "A leakage is bad and an injection is good" is wrong because:
options: The terms describe DIRECTION of flow, not virtue — today's savings finance tomorrow's investment

subtopics.title: Adding Government — Taxes In, Spending Out

questions.question: Taxes are classified as a leakage because:
options: Money collected by SARS is drawn out of the spending stream — households and firms cannot spend it

questions.question: Government spending is an injection because:
options: Salaries, roads, textbooks, medicines and grants pump public money BACK into the circle

questions.question: With households, firms and government but NO foreign trade, the economy is:
options: Still a CLOSED economy — two leakages (savings, taxes) and two injections (investment, government spending)

subtopics.title: The Foreign Sector — Opening the Economy

questions.question: Imports are a leakage because:
options: Rands earned inside our circle are paid to producers outside it — the spending exits our flow

questions.question: Citrus shipped to the Netherlands and platinum sold to Japan are classified as:
options: EXPORTS — an injection: foreign money streaming into South African firms

questions.question: The three leakages and three injections, listed completely:
options: Leakages: wages, rent, interest; injections: profit, tax, exports
Leakages: investment, spending, exports; injections: savings, taxes, imports
Leakages: SAVINGS, TAXES, IMPORTS; injections: INVESTMENT, GOVERNMENT SPENDING, EXPORTS
Leakages: imports only; injections: exports only

questions.question: "Every leakage has a matching injection through the same channel" means:
options: Leakages and injections are always equal
The financial sector handles all six flows
Three doors, traffic both ways: savings/investment through the financial sector, taxes/spending through government, imports/exports through the foreign sector

questions.question: On month-end Friday, the wage landing and moving to the supermarket, barber and hardware shows:
options: Money never resting — it CIRCLES: work out, income home, spending onward

questions.question: The "hiring side of life" and the "till side of life" are, formally:
options: The financial sector and the foreign sector
The FACTOR market — where work finds employers — and the GOODS market — where money finds goods
Two names for the same market

questions.question: Labour riding to work while wages come home illustrates:
options: The two-lane road: REAL flows one way, MONEY flows the opposite way

questions.question: Granny's R600 fixed deposit, in the water picture, is:
options: The bank DRAIN — savings stepping out of the stream

questions.question: The bakery's new mixer, financed by a bank loan, is:
options: The bank TAP — savings lent onward and returning as investment

questions.question: The "three doors" memory trick pairs:
options: Savings with exports, taxes with investment
Bank: savings/investment; government: taxes/spending; border: imports/exports
Each drain with a random tap

questions.question: "Drains are not the enemy" because:
options: Drains and taps are the same flow
The deposit granny makes is exactly the money that becomes the bakery's mixer — direction, never virtue

questions.question: When the three drains together pull out more than the three taps pour in:
options: The level falls — spending, orders, production and pay all shrink round by round

questions.question: Drains exactly equal to taps means:
options: EQUILIBRIUM — the level holds; the street calls it steady

questions.question: "Treasury announces an infrastructure programme" translates as:
options: The government TAP opening wider — an injection
A leakage through the government door

questions.question: A school buying imported projectors and a mine landing a Japanese platinum order are, in order:
options: Border DRAIN (import out), then border TAP (export in)
